ruling.recommended_action: Refer to a human reviewer to fix the scope of the rider's 17:02 'Sure, your call.' consent [F10] for the 17:04–17:11 segment before any refund is executed; if the first segment is cleared, the refund per RD-2 is 2.58 km × $1.4100/km = $3.64 on the unexempted 17:18–17:23 segment, with a driver account-review flag under RD-6 (2 upheld route disputes in 90 days) [F18].
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip with two recorded off-route segments — 17:04–17:11 adding 2.44 km [F3] and 17:18–17:23 adding 2.58 km [F4] — against an overall +5.4 km over the 16.3 km optimal route [F1]. RD-1 requires each segment to be screened separately for excuse under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 before any amount is computed under RD-2. The incident screen is settled: no traffic incident was recorded near the route in the trip window [F15], and the band-4 speeds on PIE and CTE (30–39 km/h) [F13][F14] are not the band 1–2 severe congestion RD-4(b) contemplates and cannot exempt a segment on their own; weather was fair [F16] [RD-4].

For the second segment (17:18–17:23) the record settles the question: the chat is complete and every message is timestamped, two messages in total [F11]; the rider's only message is at 17:02 [F10], sent long before this segment's 17:18 start and addressed to the jam round the start, and the driver's post-trip statement that "the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" [F12] is a statement written after the trip, not the rider's consent (G11). With no rider message in advance, this segment counts as an unexempted deviation [F4][F11][F12] [RD-5], and on a metered trip its extra kilometres enter the fare [F5][F8] [RD-2].

For the first segment (17:04–17:11) the record does not let me fix the scope of the consent. The rider's 17:02 reply "Sure, your call." [F10] is a rider message sent before the segment start, so timing is satisfied, but its reach is ambiguous: read as a general route authorisation ("your call" on how to get round the jam the driver had just described) [F9][F10] it covers a routing chosen to reach the destination and the segment would be exempt; read as consent to the named road "Bedok North Road" [F9], nothing in the fact table ties the driven track to that road or to any other road, which is the G13 case. I cannot read the words narrowly enough to make the segment refundable on this record, and the trace treats a finding on this segment as changing the amount: with it exempt the refund is $3.64, with it counting the refund would be higher. [F3][F9][F10] [RD-5]

Because an undetermined scope on a segment that changes the amount must go to a person, I do not issue the refund myself. I record the amount the human reviewer would execute if the first segment is cleared: $30.54 ÷ 21.66 km = $1.4100/km [F5][F8]; 2.58 km × $1.4100/km = $3.6378 → $3.64 [F4][F5] [RD-2]. The $0.13 waiting unit (0.5 min × $0.26/min) is metered waiting time on a RydeTAXI trip and is not refundable [F6][RD-3], and the billed excess of $7.56 for 5.36 km is not refundable beyond the identified unexempted segment [F5][RD-2].

The driver already has 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days [F18], so if the reviewer upholds the RD-2 refund the conduct becomes repeated and RD-6 attaches an account-review flag; profile facts support only that additional action, not the deviation finding itself [F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages [F9][F10] and the driver's statement [F12]. F9 is a routing question, F10 an agreement and F12 an explanation about GPS rerouting; the complaint concerns a second unagreed deviation. Nothing threatens, intimidates, harasses or alleges dangerous driving, so safety_concern = none [F9][F10][F12] [SAFE-1].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's pre-segment reply 'Sure, your call.' [F10] follows the driver's question naming 'Bedok North Road' [F9] and precedes the 17:04 start, so timing is satisfied. The scope is ambiguous: as a general route authorisation it covers a routing chosen to get round the jam (no driver's errand appears) [F9][F10]; as consent to the named road only, no fact ties the driven track to Bedok North Road or to any other road, which is the G13 case. The record does not settle the scope, and because this segment changes the amount the case goes to a person [RD-5].

The chat record is complete and fully timestamped, two messages in total [F11]. No rider message precedes the 17:18:05 start of this segment: the rider's only message is at 17:02 [F10] and addresses the round-the-jam routing near the start. The driver's post-trip sentence that the second turn-off was his GPS rerouting is a statement, not the rider's consent [F12], so this segment is unagreed and counts as an unexempted deviation [RD-1][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: The driver read 'Sure, your call.' [F10] as a general route authorisation covering the whole trip, and thus the second segment. A general authorisation covers a route chosen to reach the destination, not a separate later turn-off the rider was never asked about: F11 shows the chat ends at two messages, the rider sent nothing before 17:18, and F12 admits the second turn-off was the driver's own GPS rerouting [F10][F11][F12][RD-5].

The driver relied on PIE speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) [F13] as congestion support. Band 4 is not the band 1–2 severe congestion of RD-4(b), band evidence alone cannot exempt a segment, no traffic incident on the replaced stretch is recorded in the trip window [F15], and the band record is not tied to the stretch the 17:04–17:11 segment replaced [F13][F15][RD-4].

The rider asked for $3.64 as the refund computed on the second segment alone [F4][F5]. That arithmetic is right for that segment ($30.54 ÷ 21.66 km = $1.4100/km; 2.58 km × $1.4100/km = $3.6378 → $3.64) [F5][F8][RD-2], but the first segment's scope is undetermined and changes the amount, so no refund can be executed on this record [F3][F9][F10][RD-5].

The driver argued the remaining billed excess of $7.56 − $3.64 = $3.92 is not refundable [F5]. That is correct as to mileage outside the identified unexempted segments [F5][RD-2], but it gives the driver no relief on the live question: the first segment's scope is undetermined and is for a person to decide [F3][F9][F10][RD-5].
